Q1.branch: the set's members as sqlx reads them

Q1.P13.branch: sqlx's unqualified INSERT INTO _sqlx_migrations at the end of each migration (and its UPDATE after a commit, for later migrations): applied only when the path in force reaches the default schema with only pg_catalog or set schemas before it; a path no entry of which can hold it refused (42P01); an unknown path or entry, a set relation named _sqlx_migrations, or a statement that may drop or rename public or _sqlx_migrations not proven; the "$user" entry counts as any set schema; the INSERT runs in the transaction in force at the end of the string (a new one after the string committed sqlx's) and is refused (25006) when that transaction is read-only; the UPDATE after the commit runs in a new transaction with the session's defaults, and a committed default_transaction_read_only on (SET or SET SESSION CHARACTERISTICS) refuses it, which stops the run: every later migration is not applied

Q1.P7.branch: a numeric literal scan.l REL_17_6 refuses anywhere in a migration (an integer, numeric or real followed by an identifier character, an exponent sign without digits, 0x, 0o or 0b without digits) or two numeric constants written together (1.2.3) refuses the whole migration (42601): Postgres parses the whole string before it runs any statement

R1.branch: CREATE [OR REPLACE] [TEMP] VIEW / MATERIALIZED VIEW / SEQUENCE / TYPE / DOMAIN, CREATE TABLE AS, SELECT INTO, CREATE SCHEMA

R1.P12.branch: CREATE VIEW/SEQUENCE/TYPE/DOMAIN/SCHEMA (also R2) of a name code may have created or left behind may fail; with IF NOT EXISTS or OR REPLACE its record is uncertain

R1.P2.branch: CREATE TABLE AS, SELECT INTO and CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW: an output column name (alias, column list, or the name of a plain column reference, function call or cast) equal to a system column name refused (42701); CREATE SCHEMA of a pg_ name, also the role-named schema of AUTHORIZATION, refused (42939, Y06); a relation (table, view, materialized view, sequence, composite type, foreign table, index) created in pg_catalog or pg_toast refused (42501), any other object created in pg_catalog may fail (E6, Y07); CREATE SCHEMA, by name or by AUTHORIZATION, of a schema the set holds, or of public or information_schema under E5 unless the set dropped it, refused (42P06) and skipped with IF NOT EXISTS, and may fail when code may have created it (Y08, Y43); CREATE TYPE AS RANGE whose multirange type name (multirange_type_name, or makeMultirangeTypeName's) a pg_type entry the pass holds already takes refused (42710, Y21); a CREATE SCHEMA element qualified by another schema refused (42P15, Y32)

R1.P4.branch: CREATE SEQUENCE options: each written once (42601), signed integer constants in int8 range, AS smallint, integer or bigint, and the parameters sequence.c init_params computes (INCREMENT not 0, MINVALUE < MAXVALUE within the type's range, START and RESTART within the bounds, CACHE >= 1; 22023); OWNED BY NONE or a column of a table held under a certain name in the sequence's schema (55000, 42703); other values not proven; CREATE TYPE of a base or shell type (CREATE TYPE name, alone or with a parameter list) may fail (only a superuser may create one)

R1.P5.branch: CREATE DOMAIN: the base type's modifiers as M2.P5, one DEFAULT assignable to the base type, not NULL with NOT NULL, COLLATE on a collatable base type, each CHECK proven boolean over VALUE; other clauses not proven; CREATE TYPE AS (...): attribute type modifiers and collations as for columns (R3, R4); CREATE VIEW WITH (...) checked against the view options of reloptions.c, CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW WITH (...) against the heap ones; a check_option or WITH CHECK OPTION may fail (the pass does not prove a view automatically updatable); a composite type's attribute named twice (42701) and a domain's constraint name written twice (42710) refused

R1.P7.branch: no SELECT INTO in a view's or CREATE TABLE AS's query; a keyword a name position does not accept; CREATE SCHEMA read whole (name, AUTHORIZATION, elements by their own rows' readers) and the shell, composite and range forms of CREATE TYPE, otherwise row D

R1b.branch: the query of a view, CREATE TABLE AS or SELECT INTO, and a LANGUAGE sql body

R1b.P5.branch: the query of a view, CREATE TABLE AS or SELECT INTO, and a LANGUAGE sql body, are not proven; a LANGUAGE sql AS body only while check_function_bodies is on or unknown (off, the validator does not parse it); T024c1c: a LANGUAGE sql function's AS body that the validator parse-analyses at creation (fmgr_sql_validator) is proven in one form: named parameters and a result of pg_catalog base types, options LANGUAGE, volatility, STRICT, LEAKPROOF, SECURITY and PARALLEL only, one SELECT of one output expression of the RETURNS type over at most one table held with known columns under a certain name ([AS] alias) with an optional WHERE; a name is a column of its level's table before a parameter (an outer level's column is not proven); EXISTS of the same form, one integer subscript of a parenthesised array, pg_catalog functions the set does not overload and the platform functions of SB-M8; never after an opaque statement, an operator, cast, operator class or family, access method or aggregate of the set, or a statement naming row_security

R2.P5.branch: CREATE TYPE AS ENUM: a label written twice (23505) or longer than 63 bytes (42602) refused; a label the pass does not decode may fail

R2.P7.branch: CREATE TYPE: a keyword a name position does not accept; the whole statement read as CREATE TYPE n AS ENUM ([Sconst [, ...]] ), otherwise row D

R3.branch: ALTER TYPE n ADD VALUE [IF NOT EXISTS] 'v' [BEFORE|AFTER 'w'] / RENAME VALUE

R3.K2.branch: ADD VALUE: an existing label (without IF NOT EXISTS) or a missing BEFORE/AFTER label is refused; RENAME VALUE of a missing label or to an existing one is refused; unknown labels may fail; a label added in this transaction to a type that existed before it is unsafe to use before the commit (55P04); labels are the decoded string values, and a label written in a form the pass does not decode (octal, hexadecimal or Unicode escapes, U&'...') makes the type's labels unknown (and may be any unsafe label); ADD VALUE and RENAME VALUE of a label longer than 63 bytes refused (42602)

R3.P1.branch: ALTER TYPE: a type the set creates must be held; ADD VALUE and RENAME VALUE of a table's row type are refused, and of a name the pass does not hold as a type may fail (E1 does not cover enums)

R3.P12.branch: ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE or RENAME VALUE of a type code names (labels the pass does not see) may fail

R3.P7.branch: ALTER TYPE n ADD VALUE [IF NOT EXISTS] Sconst [{BEFORE | AFTER} Sconst] and RENAME VALUE Sconst TO Sconst read whole, otherwise row D

R4.summary: tables that use it become partial

ADD/DROP/ALTER/RENAME ATTRIBUTE of a name held as anything but a composite type, and other ALTER TYPE forms of a relation's row type are refused (a sequence or index: may fail); ALTER VIEW / MATERIALIZED VIEW ... RENAME [COLUMN] and ALTER TYPE ... RENAME ATTRIBUTE of a held name may fail (columns not tracked); ALTER DOMAIN ... DROP CONSTRAINT (without IF EXISTS), VALIDATE CONSTRAINT and RENAME CONSTRAINT may fail (E1 does not cover constraints); ALTER TYPE (other than ADD / RENAME VALUE) and ALTER DOMAIN of a name the pass does not hold as a type may fail (E1 does not cover types other than its own)
R4.P1.summary: tables that use it become partial

R4.P2.branch: ALTER TYPE ... ADD ATTRIBUTE of a system column name on a type a typed table uses: refused with CASCADE (42701), may fail otherwise; any attribute change without CASCADE on a type a typed table uses refused (2BP01)
R4.P2.summary: tables that use it become partial

R4.P4.summary: tables that use it become partial

R4.P5.summary: tables that use it become partial

R4.P7.branch: ALTER TYPE (RENAME TO, RENAME ATTRIBUTE, OWNER TO, SET SCHEMA, ADD/DROP/ALTER ATTRIBUTE), ALTER DOMAIN (AlterDomainStmt, RENAME, OWNER, SET SCHEMA), ALTER VIEW / MATERIALIZED VIEW (RENAME, RENAME COLUMN, SET SCHEMA, OWNER TO, [NO] DEPENDS ON EXTENSION, SET/RESET (...), ALTER COLUMN SET/DROP DEFAULT), ALTER SEQUENCE RENAME TO and ALTER COLLATION read whole, otherwise row D
R4.P7.summary: tables that use it become partial

R5.P4.branch: DROP <kind> of an object held as another kind is refused; DROP INDEX [IF EXISTS] of a name held as another relation kind is refused (42809)

R5.P7.branch: DROP {TYPE | DOMAIN | VIEW | MATERIALIZED VIEW | SEQUENCE | COLLATION | ...} [IF EXISTS] names [CASCADE | RESTRICT], DROP {FUNCTION | PROCEDURE | ROUTINE | AGGREGATE | OPERATOR} with argument types, DROP CAST read whole, otherwise row D

RENAME TO; its array and multirange names): every statement that can create an object with a pg_depend dependency adds an entry with the identity of its object and every word it writes (strings included; a routine's or DO body's DDL, or the whole body when it is not read or dynamic; a regclass-family type with a numeric constant names every object), no word removed; three positions are proven no dependency: the entry's own created name, the ON-table of an object of a table when a relation of that name is dropped, and a REFERENCES target the foreign-key record decides (a held table with known facts); an entry ends only when the object of its identity is removed: DROP of it (a trigger or policy by name and table; a routine without an argument list only when it has one held identity), DROP of its table, CREATE OR REPLACE of the same identity; a DROP that removes nothing ends none, and a rename moves the identity to the new name; the sequences a table's columns own (serial, identity, OWNED BY; the generated name clipped as ChooseRelationName does, with any numeric suffix) are names of the table; a statement that copies columns (CREATE TABLE AS, SELECT INTO, LIKE, INHERITS, PARTITION OF, OF, ALTER TABLE ... INHERIT, and views and materialized views) names the copied columns' types as the pass holds them, or every type when it does not, so DROP TYPE and DROP DOMAIN may fail while it is live; DROP SCHEMA also while the search_path may resolve to it; after DROP ... CASCADE the objects such entries created are no longer held and their CREATE or use may fail, and their entries stay live; DROP ... CASCADE of a table, view, type or domain drops every held table's column whose type is a dropped type, its array, or a domain or range over it (under any name it has had) with M5b's CASCADE effects, the table partial when the column's type or the dropped type is not exact; a partition-key column takes its table (M6 CASCADE), and the statement may fail when that is not exact

R6.branch: CREATE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE, ALTER FUNCTION/PROCEDURE/ROUTINE ... [RENAME TO g]

R6.P1.branch: CREATE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE: the language must exist; sql and plpgsql (an identifier folded, or a string constant spelled exactly so) are proven, every other language may fail

R6.P12.branch: CREATE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE without OR REPLACE of a routine code may have created, and DROP of a routine code names, may fail; a routine code creates, replaces, alters or drops has unknown definitions (R6.P3)

R6.P14.branch: CREATE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE ... LANGUAGE plpgsql: the validator refuses a pseudo-type result other than trigger, event_trigger, record, void and the polymorphic types and a pseudo-type argument other than record and the polymorphic types (0A000), LANGUAGE sql a pseudo-type result other than record, void and the polymorphic types and a pseudo-type input argument other than the polymorphic types (42P13), a function without RETURNS and OUT parameters is refused (42P13); with check_function_bodies on or unknown the body is compiled and applied only in the provable subset (one block [<<l>>] [DECLARE name type [:= expr];...] BEGIN ... [EXCEPTION WHEN cond [OR cond] THEN ...] END [l] [;]; assignments to declared variables, parameters and NEW/OLD.col of a trigger function, RETURN per make_return_stmt, IF/ELSIF/ELSE, NULL, RAISE [level] 'fmt' [, expr], EXECUTE expr, PERFORM query, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE of the expression reader's subset, statements the V7 readers read completely, T024c1b: SELECT with at most one INTO [STRICT] at parenthesis depth 0 whose targets are parameters or declared variables (several only of a pg_catalog type that is not composite) and the rest a query of the syntax-only reader; declared names may be unreserved SQL keywords; expressions of the syntax-only reader, whose FROM items are relations or, T024c1b, function calls); a certain compile error inside it (end label, trailing text, duplicate declaration, unknown variable, NEW.x outside a trigger function, RETURN against the result, RAISE parameter count, unknown condition, bad SQLSTATE, serial declared type, a trigger function with parameters) refused, anything else may fail

R6.P2.branch: ALTER FUNCTION, PROCEDURE or ROUTINE ... RENAME TO g: refused (42723) when the set holds g with the same argument types in the same schema; may fail when the argument types or the held routines are not proven

R6.P3.branch: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE over a held routine of the same identity (schema, name, input types of pg_catalog): kind (42809), return type and SETOF, OUT/INOUT/TABLE columns, named input parameters, and at least its defaults kept (42P13), else refused; an identity the pass cannot decide (types outside pg_catalog, a schema not proven, a routine changed by a statement not read) not proven

R6.P4.branch: functions and procedures: the kind a statement names must be the kind the set holds; the options of CREATE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE at most once each except SET (42601), volatility, STRICT, LEAKPROOF, COST, ROWS and PARALLEL refused for a procedure (42P13), COST and ROWS positive constants, ROWS only for a set-returning function (22023), PARALLEL SAFE, RESTRICTED or UNSAFE, a SET clause proven as N2.P5 proves SET; TRANSFORM, WINDOW, SUPPORT and options not read may fail; the actions of ALTER FUNCTION, PROCEDURE and ROUTINE as the CREATE options (an option twice, function attributes on a procedure, COST and ROWS, PARALLEL), against the one held definition when the pass read it; ROWS, and a ROUTINE's function attributes, on a routine not read may fail; a function or procedure with LEAKPROOF or SUPPORT, or in a language other than plpgsql and sql (c, internal, the untrusted procedural languages), may fail (only a superuser may create it); E6: ALTER FUNCTION, PROCEDURE, ROUTINE or AGGREGATE ... OWNER TO a role the set created may fail

R6.P5.branch: CREATE FUNCTION and PROCEDURE: a polymorphic result or OUT parameter that no input determines refused (42P13; check_valid_polymorphic_signature: anyrange and anymultirange need an anyrange or anymultirange input, the other anyelement-family types any of that family, anycompatiblerange and anycompatiblemultirange an input of those two, the other anycompatible-family types any of that family, internal an internal input; Y17); a type modifier on an argument, OUT, RETURNS or RETURNS TABLE type as M2.P5 (42601 when the type takes none; Y18); the SET values of ALTER FUNCTION, PROCEDURE and ROUTINE as N2.P1 and N2.P5

R6.P7.branch: CREATE/ALTER FUNCTION/PROCEDURE: an unqualified routine name is a type_function_name (no col_name or reserved keyword); ALTER FUNCTION/PROCEDURE/ROUTINE read whole as RENAME TO, OWNER TO, SET SCHEMA, [NO] DEPENDS ON EXTENSION or alterfunc_opt_list [RESTRICT], otherwise row D

T1.summary: nothing changes, or the P6 effect

T1.P4.summary: nothing changes, or the P6 effect

T1.P6.summary: nothing changes, or the P6 effect

T1.P7.summary: nothing changes, or the P6 effect
